# A feasible shared-plane corner fill with strict mixed-depth descent

This note supplies an exact first-variation mechanism in the same family
that disproves ordinary-deficit control of simplex-container costs. Large
compatibility-driven added mass can help a depth-lowering deformation when
it enters fibers outside the active cap budget. It does not establish a
descent direction at an arbitrary attained bad minimizer.

## 1. An exact feasible family in a fixed shared-plane class

Let T=conv(0,e1,e2), fix a sufficiently small ε>0, and write

    b=ε², a=1+b, ε/2≤s≤ε,
    A_s={x,y≥0:s≤x+y≤1},
    P_s={x≤a,y≤a,x+y≥s}, B=bT.

The actual three fibers at integer bases 0,1,2 are

    K0=A_s, K1=P_s/2, K2=B.                                 (1)

Compatibility follows because A_s+B⊂P_s. More strongly, they admit the
following FIXED nine-plane shared representation, with integer coordinate z:

    x≤1−(1−b)z/2,             y≤1−(1−b)z/2,
    x≥−(a−s)z/2,              x≥−(a−s)(2−z)/2,
    y≥−(a−s)z/2,              y≥−(a−s)(2−z)/2,
    x+y≥s(1−z/2),
    x+y≤1+bz,                 x+y≤2+b−z.                    (2)

Together with 0≤z≤2, this is a bounded full-dimensional convex body.
At z=0 the extra inequalities in (2) are redundant and give exactly A_s.
At z=1, they give x,y≤a/2, x+y≥s/2; the individual lower bounds
x,y≥(s−a)/2 and the sum upper bound x+y≤a follow from those three
inequalities. At z=2 the system is exactly x,y≥0, x+y≤b. Thus every
asserted fiber in (1) is actual.

Every continuous normal in (2) is fixed and nonzero. Decreasing s
relaxes its four individual-coordinate lower bounds and its sum lower
bound throughout 0≤z≤2, while leaving the other planes fixed. Hence
this is a genuine simultaneous feasible deformation of shared ambient
planes in a fixed finite-complexity class. No independent fiber
translation, affine lattice distortion, or compatibility repair is used.

## 2. Exact global depth and its unique active integer base

Take ε≤1/16 and also smaller than the uniform local truncation radius
in `candidate 3795aff5f3322d52`.
That proved theorem gives the exact ordinary absolute maximal depth of A_s:

    f(s)=(1+sqrt(1+3s²))/9−s²/3.                             (3)

Its unique maximizer is (t_s,t_s), where

    t_s=(1+sqrt(1+3s²))/6.

This point belongs to A_s. The only dependency of this section on an
ordinary stability result is the already proved exact local truncation
formula; no uniform claim about arbitrary bodies is being substituted.

Base 0 is exposed. Any continuous cap through a point of A_s can be
extended with a sufficiently large finite integer tilt that excludes the
other two bounded fibers. Therefore the restricted mixed-depth maximum
at base 0 is exactly f(s), with no other-fiber contribution.

For every candidate in the middle triangle P_s/2, an ordinary canonical
triangle cap has mass at most (4/9)|P_s/2|. A sufficiently large finite
integer tilt can exclude A_s and include B, without changing the middle
cap. Thus its restricted mixed-depth maximum is at most

    U(s)=(4/9)|P_s/2|+|B|=(2a−s)²/18+b²/2.                  (4)

These are genuine ambient halfspaces, and (4) is an upper cover for every
middle candidate, not a calculation at a prescribed centroid. At exposed
base 2 the restricted maximum is (4/9)|B|=2b²/9.

The gap from (3) to (4) is strictly positive uniformly over the stated
s-interval. Since sqrt(1+3s²)≥1,

    f(s)−U(s)
      ≥2s/9−7s²/18−4b/9−13b²/18
      ≥ε/9−5ε²/6−13ε⁴/18
      ≥ε/9−ε²
      ≥7ε/144>0.                                            (5)

The penultimate step uses ε²≤1/256, which makes 5/6+13ε²/18<1.
Also f(s)>1/5>2b²/9. Consequently the unique active integer base is 0,
and the global normalized mixed depth is exactly

    D(s)=f(s)/M(s),
    M(s)=(1−s²)/2+(2a−s)²/8+b²/2.                           (6)

The lower bound implicit in this equality holds for all closed ambient
halfspaces because the own-fiber maximum (3) already supplies f(s).
The matching upper bounds in every fiber were obtained with finite
actual ambient tilts. No oblique direction has been omitted.

## 3. Exact first variation and strict sign

Parameterize the fill by decreasing s, so its time derivative is ds/dt=−1.
Differentiating the exact formulas gives

    d f/dt = (s/3)[2−1/sqrt(1+3s²)] ≤2s/3,
    d M/dt = (2a+3s)/4 ≥1/2.                                (7)

For ε≤1/16, one has f(s)>1/5 and M(s)<2. Therefore

    (d f/dt)M − f(d M/dt)
       ≤4s/3−1/10
       ≤1/12−1/10=−1/60.

The exact normalized derivative satisfies

    dD/dt ≤−1/[60 M(s)²] < −1/240.                          (8)

Thus this shared-plane deformation strictly lowers the full maximum
over every actual mixed candidate, while filling the nonsimplex corner
of the active fiber. The theorem applies on the entire interval from
s=ε to s=ε/2, which suffices for a nonzero compatible descent.

This is compatible with the earlier cost obstruction: the ordinary
fiber defect is quadratic in s, whereas the middle triangle gains mass
at first order when its contact plane is relaxed. In the present phase
that extra mass does not become an active candidate budget. Its effect
on the normalization outweighs the increase in the active fiber's
absolute depth.

## 4. The general finite-active-base first-variation invariant

Here is the precise abstract implication illustrated above. Let a
one-sided feasible deformation of finitely many positive actual fibers
have total mass M(t)=M_0+t m+o(t). Let Q_p(t) be its restricted absolute
maximum depth at base p, and suppose these functions are continuous at
zero. Let Q_0=max_p Q_p(0), D_0=Q_0/M_0, and I={p:Q_p(0)=Q_0}.
Suppose for p∈I there are valid all-candidate upper expansions

    Q_p(t)≤Q_0+t a_p+o(t).                                  (9)

Then

    limsup_(t↓0) [D(t)−D_0]/t
       ≤ [max_(p∈I) a_p − D_0 m]/M_0.                       (10)

Indeed the finitely many inactive bases have a strict gap at zero and
remain inactive for small t by continuity. Taking the maximum of the
finitely many upper expansions (9) and dividing by M(t) proves (10).
No limit is interchanged with an unbounded cap family: (9) must already
control every candidate and cap at each active base.

Thus a sufficient strict-descent invariant is

    max_(p∈I) a_p < D_0 m.                                  (11)

In the explicit family, I={0}, a_0 is the first expression in (7), and
m is the second; (8) verifies (11). This is a comparison of actual active
cap flux with total added mass, rather than a bound on total added mass
by ordinary depth deficits.

## 5. Exact limitation at an attained bad minimizer

The supplied ordinary simplex stability theorem controls a fiber's own
depth deficit and its simplex approximation. It does not furnish the
simultaneously feasible velocity or the all-active-base expansions (9)
needed for (11). The arbitrary-container obstruction shows that one
cannot replace these requirements by a bound on compatibility repair
mass. The example here shows additionally that a large repair mass can
have the favorable sign when it remains outside the active budgets.

The unresolved statement is therefore **simultaneous active-base cap-flux
descent**: under the hypothesis of an attained bad compatible-family
minimum, find one actual shared-plane velocity and valid expansions (9)
that satisfy (11), or an appropriate zero-derivative rigidity statement.
This is a theorem-strength missing lemma and remains blocked. No assertion
of its validity is included here. The concrete new invariant is (10)–(11),
with a fully certified nontrivial realization in (1)–(8); further attempts
must control its entire active-base maximum, not merely separate ordinary
fiber deficits.
